case_name: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board & Anr v M/S Prakash Dal Mill & Ors
petitioner: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board & Anr
facts: The Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (hereinafter referred to as 'appellant No.1) had formed an industrial layout at Tarihal village in the year 1983, pursuant to which, it invited interested purchasers to make applications for allotment of industrial sites.
Pursuant to the same, the respondents herein, applied for the allotment of sites.
It is a matter of record that the respondents had applied for the allotment of sites at different points of time.
Consequently, the appellant issued letters of intent, indicating that it had resolved to allot all respondents the sites shown in their cause titles at Tarihal Industrial Estate.
The said letter also indicated the tentative price at which the land was sought to be allotted.
issues: Whether the High Court committed a grave error in holding that Cl. 7(b) of the lease-cum-sale agreement doesn't confer power on the appellants to revise or alter the tentative price.
Whether the final allotment price fixed by the appellant was reasonable, arbitrary, unjust and contrary to what was legitimately expected and assured by the appellant.
petitioner_arguments: The High Court committed a grave error in holding that Cl. 7(b) of the lease-cum-sale agreement doesn't confer power on the appellants to revise or alter the tentative price.
The final allotment price fixed by the appellant was reasonable, based on the cost of acquisition, development expenditure, statutory charges and interest.
The respondents have wrongly claimed that they had been allotted plots in fully developed area.
respondent_arguments: The allotment letters have been issued by the appellant Board in exercise of its powers u/s. 41 of the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966.
The final allotment price fixed by the appellant was unreasonable, arbitrary, unjust and contrary to what was legitimately expected and assured by the appellant.
court_reasoning: The power of fixation of price of the land vested with the appellant.
The final price fixed was much less than the actual market price and hence the High Court erred in holding that it was arbitrary, unjust and unfair.
The present matter was not one of escalation of price but the fixation of the final price.
holding: The Division Bench of the High Court allowed the writ appeal by setting aside the judgment of the High Court in W.P. Nos. 23578 to 23617 of 1999 dated 7th July, 1999.
Hence the instant appeals by special leave before us.
